segments.he: מַעֲלַת הַמְּלִיצָה בַּשִּׂיחָה בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ
segments.en: In truth, now, in exile after the destruction of the Holy Temple, it is very difficult to rejoice — except through the power of the Tzaddikim who possess great and wondrous daas [knowledge-consciousness] that is considered like the building of the Holy Temple — as our Sages, of blessed memory, said: "Whoever possesses daas..." They draw down joy upon us in Him, may He be blessed, so that we can sustain ourselves in this bitter exile.

segments.he: עִנְיָן זֶה שֶׁל מַעֲלַת הַמְּלִיצָה הוּא נִצְרָךְ מְאד לְכָל אָדָם הֶחָפֵץ חַיִּים אֲמִתִּיִּים וְנִצְחִיִּים. הָרוֹצֶה לָגֶשֶׁת אֶל הַקּדֶשׁ לֵילֵךְ בְּדַרְכֵי ה' לָשׁוּב אֵלָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ. אֲשֶׁר הָעֵצָה הַכְּלָלִיִּית שֶׁהִוא יְסוֹד כָּל הָעֵצוֹת. הִוא הַהִתְבּוֹדְדוּת וְהַשִּׂיחָה בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ כַּמְבאָר אֶצְלֵנוּ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים. דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁיַּרְגִּיל עַצְמוֹ בְּכָל יוֹם לֵילֵךְ לְמָקוֹם מְיֻחָד לְהִתְבּוֹדֵד שָׁם וּלְפָרֵשׁ שִׂיחָתוֹ לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ כַּאֲשֶׁר יְדַבֵּר אִישׁ אֶל רֵעֵהוּ. וּלְהַרְבּוֹת בִּטְעָנוֹת וְהַפְצָרוֹת וּבַקָּשׁוֹת וּפִיּוּסִים בַּלָּשׁוֹן שֶׁמְּדַבְּרִים בּוֹ. (דְּהַיְנוּ בִּמְדִינָתֵנוּ בִּלְשׁוֹן אַשְׁכְּנַז שֶׁאָנוּ מְדַבְּרִים בּוֹ): שֶׁיַּעַזְרֵהוּ ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וִיזַכֵּהוּ לָשׁוּב מִמַּעֲשָׂיו הָרָעִים וּלְהִתְקָרֵב אֵלָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכוּ'.
segments.en: And therefore [Rochel] his mother called him Ben Oni [son of my suffering]. For Rochel died then and was buried at the crossroads so that Israel could weep upon her grave at the time of the destruction — as our Sages, of blessed memory, said. And therefore, because our mother Rochel saw the great destruction that would come before we merit the final redemption — therefore she called his name Ben Oni, on account of the great mourning and weeping that is needed every night — to weep over the destruction of the Holy Temple. And so must every person cry and weep greatly every day for his own blemishes that delay the building of the Holy Temple. This is the aspect of "A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping — Rochel weeping for her children" [Yirmeyahu 31:15]. But his father [Yaakov] called him Binyamin — on account of the Land of Israel. For Yaakov called him ben yamin [son of the right, son of the south] — on account of the end, that we will return to the Land of Israel, where the Holy Temple will be built in the portion of Binyamin, where the source of joy is.

segments.he: וּלְעִנְיָן זֶה הוּא דָּבָר גָּדוֹל עִנְיַן הַמְּלִיצָה. דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁיַּרְגִּיל עַצְמוֹ לְהַרְחִיב שִׂיחָתוֹ וּלְהַרְבּוֹת בִּטְעָנוֹת וּלְבַקֵּשׁ לִמְצא לְעַצְמוֹ בְּכָל פַּעַם דִּבְרֵי תַּחֲנוּנִים וּפִיּוּסִים חֲדָשִׁים וּטְעָנוֹת נָאוֹת וְדִבְרֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת שֶׁל רַחֲמִים הַרְבֵּה. כְּדֶרֶךְ הַמַּפְצִירִים. כְּדֶרֶךְ הַבָּאִים לִפְנֵי מְלָכִים וְשׁוֹפְטִים לְהִתְחַנֵּן עַל נַפְשָׁם כְּשֶׁיּוֹדְעִים בְּעַצְמָם שֶׁהֵם חַיָּבִים וְהֵם בָּאִים לְפַיְּסָם. שֶׁאָז מִגּדֶל מְרִירוּת נַפְשָׁם יוֹצֵא מִלִּבָּם מִמֵּילָא דִּבְרֵי תַּחֲנוּנִים וּפִיּוּסִים הַרְבֵּה עַד שֶׁלִּפְעָמִים מְעוֹרְרִים לֵב הַמֶּלֶךְ אוֹ הַשּׁוֹפֵט עַד שֶׁמַּתְחִיל לִבְכּוֹת עִמָּהֶם גַּם כֵּן מִגּדֶל הָרַחֲמָנוּת וְכַיּוֹצֵא בְּדִבּוּרִים אֵלֶּה הַרְבֵּה. כִּי לְעִנְיַן שִׂיחָה בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ. שֶׁהִוא עִקַּר הַתַּכְלִית הָאֱמֶת שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לִזְכּוֹת עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְחַיִּים נִצְחִיִּים לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד וּלְנֶצַח נְצָחִים.
segments.en: That is, Yaakov said: even now one must call him Binyamin — on account of the Land of Israel, which is the aspect of joy. For even now, in exile, it is forbidden to be in sadness — rather one must cry and weep and pour out one's speech for a designated hour or two during the day. But for all the rest of the day one must be in joy — to gladden one's soul through all the paths of counsel. For through joy is the essential clarification from the heichalos [chambers] of the [spiritual] permutations — and through this precisely one exits from exile each according to one's own level, in the aspect of: "for with joy you shall go forth" [Yeshayahu 55:12].

segments.he: וּלְהִנָּצֵל מִבְּאֵר שַׁחַת וּמִטִּיט הַיָּוֵן וְכוּ' וְכוּ'. לְעִנְיָן זֶה צְרִיכִין כָּל מִינֵי דִּבּוּרִים שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם תְּחִנּוֹת וּבַקָּשׁוֹת וְרִצּוּיִים וּפִיּוּסִים וְהַפְצָרוֹת וְרַחֲמָנוּת וַחֲנִינָה וּטְעָנוֹת וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּזֶה הַרְבֵּה. וְכָל עִנְיְנֵי דִּבּוּרִים אֵלֶּה וְכָאֵלֶּה הֵם כֻּלָּם כְּלוּלִים בִּבְחִינַת מְלִיצָה. כִּי כָּל זֶה נִמְשָׁךְ בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ מִבְּחִינַת מְלִיצָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה שֶׁמִּשָּׁם יָסַד דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם סֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים בְּרוּחַ קָדְשׁוֹ שֶׁזָּכָה עַל יְדֵי רוּחַ קָדְשׁוֹ לִמְלִיצָה דִּקְדֻשָּׁה בֶּאֱמֶת.
segments.en: One can sense with one's own eyes that the chief incitement of the ayin hara [the evil eye] — which encompasses all those who dispute and oppose the Truth, whether from among the nations or from Israel in whatever form — is directed primarily against the matter of specific, detailed remembrance. That is, against what the true Tzaddikim teach us: the straight and genuine paths, in accordance with the holy Torah, of how to draw upon ourselves this zikharon [remembrance] in its particulars. Against this, they agitate and dispute, saying that this is not the way — they want everyone to go in their own way, wasting days in mockery and empty words and in perpetually chasing money and the like, and they cloak the lie in some appearance of truth, as if their intentions were for the sake of Heaven.

segments.he: עַד שֶׁזָּכָה שֶׁסִּפְרוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ סֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים כָּלוּל מִכָּל לְשׁוֹנוֹת הַמְּלִיצָה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה, וְעַל כֵּן בֶּאֱמֶת יֵשׁ לוֹ כּחַ גָּדוֹל לְעוֹרֵר לֵב הָאָדָם וּלְעוֹרֵר רַחֲמִים הָעֶלְיוֹנִים כְּשֶׁאוֹמְרִים אוֹתוֹ בְּכַוָּנַת הַלֵּב וּלְקָרֵב אֶת הָאָדָם לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ... וְעִקַּר מַעֲלַת הַמְּלִיצָה הוּא בִּשְׁבִיל הַתַּכְלִית הָאֲמִתִּי לִזְכּוֹת לְהִתְקָרֵב עַל יָדָהּ לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ. וּמִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לִמְלִיצָה כָּזאת וּמְבַלֶּה יָמָיו לְהַמְלִיץ דְּבָרָיו לִפְנֵי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּתְפִלָּה וְתַחֲנוּנִים וְכוּ' אוֹ לְהַמְלִיץ דְּבָרָיו לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְעוֹרְרָם לַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת. בְּוַדַּאי אַשְׁרֵי לוֹ אַשְׁרֵי חֶלְקוֹ. וּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה לָזֶה בִּשְׁלֵמוּת אֵינוֹ מעקב לַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ. כִּי אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּא בִּטְרוּנְיָא עִם בְּרִיּוֹתָיו. וְאֵינוֹ חָפֵץ מֵהָאָדָם שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה מַה שֶּׁאֵין בִּיכָלְתּוֹ. וְיָכוֹל לְהִתְקָרֵב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי שִׂיחָתוֹ אֵיךְ שֶׁהוּא וְאֵיךְ שֶׁיְּדַבֵּר יִהְיֶה נֶחְשָׁב בְּעֵינֵי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ לִמְלִיצָה יָפָה וְנָאָה. כִּי אֵצֶל ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הָעִקָּר הוּא הָאֱמֶת שֶׁיְּהֵא כַּוָּנַת לִבּוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת. כִּי אַחַר כַּוָּנַת הַלֵּב הֵן הֵן הַדְּבָרִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תְּהִלִּים קמ"ה) קָרוֹב ה' לְכָל קרְאָיו לְכָל אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָאוּהוּ בֶּאֱמֶת. וּמִי שֶׁמְּכַוֵּן לִבּוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת. אֲזַי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵלִיץ וְלא לָמַד דַּרְכֵי הַמְּלִיצָה מֵעוֹלָם. אַף עַל פִּי כֵן מִמֵּילָא נִפְתָּח פִּיו וְלִבּוֹ. וְיוּכַל לְדַבֵּר דִּבּוּרִים נָאִים וּטְעָנוֹת נְכוֹנוֹת לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכוּ'. שֶׁהֵם נִמְשָׁכִים מִבְּחִינַת מְלִיצָה דִּקְדֻשָּׁה.
segments.en: But one who truly takes to heart the remembrance of the World to Come — genuinely and faithfully — will certainly understand, even in specific terms, which is the straight path to walk in: whether to waste one's days in what they waste them in, G-d have mercy; or to spend one's days in hisbodidus, Torah, prayer, and crying out to Hashem — as the true Tzaddikim have taught us.

Speech carries immensely powerful force to transform a person from bad to good, for the essential victory in life's war is achieved through speech — it is Israel's primary weapon. As our Sages taught: "Our strength is only in the mouth." And this is the essential weapon of Moshiach, which is embodied by all the true Tzaddikim in whom all of Israel are included and contained. For all the weaponry of Moshiach is solely through prayer — which operates through speech — as is written in Torah 2 of Likutay Moharan and in many other places. Through this is accomplished the essential subjugation of the ayin hara, from which comes forgetfulness. For the nullification of forgetfulness and the attainment of genuine zikharon [remembrance] come through speech — "remember by mouth" — as our Sages taught. Just as one sees with one's own eyes that by reviewing one's learning many times with full speech, one always remembers it — so too with regard to the essential remembrance described above, of the World to Come, against which the ayin hara contends, seeking to erase it from the heart: the remedy is to review this remembrance through verbal speech. One should accustom oneself each day to speak aloud, with full voice, about the matter of this zikharon — to speak to one's own heart and remind oneself in full speech: "What will become of me in the World to Come? What is my ultimate end? Did I come here to set myself up permanently in this world, G-d forbid? This world passes and races by and vanishes. I came here only to prepare myself for the World to Come." And for this purpose one must study mussar books that are founded upon the words of our Sages in the Gemara and Midrashim and upon the teachings of true Tzaddikim, for all genuine mussar books speak of the purpose of the World to Come. Likewise one must practice hisbodidus each day, speaking aloud about the purpose of the World to Come, as stated. For speech has great power to remind the person, as above. And this is the meaning of: "Whenever I speak of him, I remember him more and more" [Yirmeyahu 31:19].

aligned_segments.he: וּלְהַרְבּוֹת בִּטְעָנוֹת וְהַפְצָרוֹת וּבַקָּשׁוֹת וּפִיּוּסִים בַּלָּשׁוֹן שֶׁמְּדַבְּרִים בּוֹ. (דְּהַיְנוּ בִּמְדִינָתֵנוּ בִּלְשׁוֹן אַשְׁכְּנַז שֶׁאָנוּ מְדַבְּרִים בּוֹ):
aligned_segments.en: But his father [Yaakov] called him Binyamin — on account of the Land of Israel.

aligned_segments.he: שֶׁיַּעַזְרֵהוּ ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וִיזַכֵּהוּ לָשׁוּב מִמַּעֲשָׂיו הָרָעִים וּלְהִתְקָרֵב אֵלָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכוּ'.
aligned_segments.en: For Yaakov called him ben yamin [son of the right, son of the south] — on account of the end, that we will return to the Land of Israel, where the Holy Temple will be built in the portion of Binyamin, where the source of joy is.

aligned_segments.he: וּלְעִנְיָן זֶה הוּא דָּבָר גָּדוֹל עִנְיַן הַמְּלִיצָה.
aligned_segments.en: That is, Yaakov said: even now one must call him Binyamin — on account of the Land of Israel, which is the aspect of joy.

aligned_segments.he: דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁיַּרְגִּיל עַצְמוֹ לְהַרְחִיב שִׂיחָתוֹ וּלְהַרְבּוֹת בִּטְעָנוֹת וּלְבַקֵּשׁ לִמְצא לְעַצְמוֹ בְּכָל פַּעַם דִּבְרֵי תַּחֲנוּנִים וּפִיּוּסִים חֲדָשִׁים וּטְעָנוֹת נָאוֹת וְדִבְרֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת שֶׁל רַחֲמִים הַרְבֵּה. כְּדֶרֶךְ הַמַּפְצִירִים.
aligned_segments.en: For even now, in exile, it is forbidden to be in sadness — rather one must cry and weep and pour out one's speech for a designated hour or two during the day.

aligned_segments.he: כְּדֶרֶךְ הַבָּאִים לִפְנֵי מְלָכִים וְשׁוֹפְטִים לְהִתְחַנֵּן עַל נַפְשָׁם כְּשֶׁיּוֹדְעִים בְּעַצְמָם שֶׁהֵם חַיָּבִים וְהֵם בָּאִים לְפַיְּסָם. שֶׁאָז מִגּדֶל מְרִירוּת נַפְשָׁם יוֹצֵא מִלִּבָּם מִמֵּילָא דִּבְרֵי תַּחֲנוּנִים וּפִיּוּסִים הַרְבֵּה עַד שֶׁלִּפְעָמִים מְעוֹרְרִים לֵב הַמֶּלֶךְ אוֹ הַשּׁוֹפֵט עַד שֶׁמַּתְחִיל לִבְכּוֹת עִמָּהֶם גַּם כֵּן מִגּדֶל הָרַחֲמָנוּת וְכַיּוֹצֵא בְּדִבּוּרִים אֵלֶּה הַרְבֵּה.
aligned_segments.en: But for all the rest of the day one must be in joy — to gladden one's soul through all the paths of counsel.

aligned_segments.he: כִּי לְעִנְיַן שִׂיחָה בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין קוֹנוֹ. שֶׁהִוא עִקַּר הַתַּכְלִית הָאֱמֶת שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לִזְכּוֹת עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְחַיִּים נִצְחִיִּים לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד וּלְנֶצַח נְצָחִים.
aligned_segments.en: For through joy is the essential clarification from the heichalos [chambers] of the [spiritual] permutations — and through this precisely one exits from exile each according to one's own level, in the aspect of: "for with joy you shall go forth" [Yeshayahu 55:12].

aligned_segments.he: וּלְהִנָּצֵל מִבְּאֵר שַׁחַת וּמִטִּיט הַיָּוֵן וְכוּ' וְכוּ'.
aligned_segments.en: One can sense with one's own eyes that the chief incitement of the ayin hara [the evil eye] — which encompasses all those who dispute and oppose the Truth, whether from among the nations or from Israel in whatever form — is directed primarily against the matter of specific, detailed remembrance.

aligned_segments.he: לְעִנְיָן זֶה צְרִיכִין כָּל מִינֵי דִּבּוּרִים שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם תְּחִנּוֹת וּבַקָּשׁוֹת וְרִצּוּיִים וּפִיּוּסִים וְהַפְצָרוֹת וְרַחֲמָנוּת וַחֲנִינָה וּטְעָנוֹת וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּזֶה הַרְבֵּה.
aligned_segments.en: That is, against what the true Tzaddikim teach us: the straight and genuine paths, in accordance with the holy Torah, of how to draw upon ourselves this zikharon [remembrance] in its particulars.

aligned_segments.he: וְכָל עִנְיְנֵי דִּבּוּרִים אֵלֶּה וְכָאֵלֶּה הֵם כֻּלָּם כְּלוּלִים בִּבְחִינַת מְלִיצָה. כִּי כָּל זֶה נִמְשָׁךְ בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹ מִבְּחִינַת מְלִיצָה הָעֶלְיוֹנָה שֶׁמִּשָּׁם יָסַד דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם סֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים בְּרוּחַ קָדְשׁוֹ שֶׁזָּכָה עַל יְדֵי רוּחַ קָדְשׁוֹ לִמְלִיצָה דִּקְדֻשָּׁה בֶּאֱמֶת.
aligned_segments.en: Against this, they agitate and dispute, saying that this is not the way — they want everyone to go in their own way, wasting days in mockery and empty words and in perpetually chasing money and the like, and they cloak the lie in some appearance of truth, as if their intentions were for the sake of Heaven.

aligned_segments.he: עַד שֶׁזָּכָה שֶׁסִּפְרוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ סֵפֶר תְּהִלִּים כָּלוּל מִכָּל לְשׁוֹנוֹת הַמְּלִיצָה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה, וְעַל כֵּן בֶּאֱמֶת יֵשׁ לוֹ כּחַ גָּדוֹל לְעוֹרֵר לֵב הָאָדָם וּלְעוֹרֵר רַחֲמִים הָעֶלְיוֹנִים כְּשֶׁאוֹמְרִים אוֹתוֹ בְּכַוָּנַת הַלֵּב וּלְקָרֵב אֶת הָאָדָם לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ... וְעִקַּר מַעֲלַת הַמְּלִיצָה הוּא בִּשְׁבִיל הַתַּכְלִית הָאֲמִתִּי לִזְכּוֹת לְהִתְקָרֵב עַל יָדָהּ לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ. וּמִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לִמְלִיצָה כָּזאת וּמְבַלֶּה יָמָיו לְהַמְלִיץ דְּבָרָיו לִפְנֵי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּתְפִלָּה וְתַחֲנוּנִים וְכוּ' אוֹ לְהַמְלִיץ דְּבָרָיו לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לְעוֹרְרָם לַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת. בְּוַדַּאי אַשְׁרֵי לוֹ אַשְׁרֵי חֶלְקוֹ. וּמִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה לָזֶה בִּשְׁלֵמוּת אֵינוֹ מעקב לַעֲבוֹדָתוֹ. כִּי אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בָּא בִּטְרוּנְיָא עִם בְּרִיּוֹתָיו. וְאֵינוֹ חָפֵץ מֵהָאָדָם שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה מַה שֶּׁאֵין בִּיכָלְתּוֹ. וְיָכוֹל לְהִתְקָרֵב לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל יְדֵי שִׂיחָתוֹ אֵיךְ שֶׁהוּא וְאֵיךְ שֶׁיְּדַבֵּר יִהְיֶה נֶחְשָׁב בְּעֵינֵי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ לִמְלִיצָה יָפָה וְנָאָה. כִּי אֵצֶל ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ הָעִקָּר הוּא הָאֱמֶת שֶׁיְּהֵא כַּוָּנַת לִבּוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת. כִּי אַחַר כַּוָּנַת הַלֵּב הֵן הֵן הַדְּבָרִים כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תְּהִלִּים קמ"ה) קָרוֹב ה' לְכָל קרְאָיו לְכָל אֲשֶׁר יִקְרָאוּהוּ בֶּאֱמֶת. וּמִי שֶׁמְּכַוֵּן לִבּוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת. אֲזַי אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵלִיץ וְלא לָמַד דַּרְכֵי הַמְּלִיצָה מֵעוֹלָם. אַף עַל פִּי כֵן מִמֵּילָא נִפְתָּח פִּיו וְלִבּוֹ. וְיוּכַל לְדַבֵּר דִּבּוּרִים נָאִים וּטְעָנוֹת נְכוֹנוֹת לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכוּ'. שֶׁהֵם נִמְשָׁכִים מִבְּחִינַת מְלִיצָה דִּקְדֻשָּׁה.
aligned_segments.en: But one who truly takes to heart the remembrance of the World to Come — genuinely and faithfully — will certainly understand, even in specific terms, which is the straight path to walk in: whether to waste one's days in what they waste them in, G-d have mercy; or to spend one's days in hisbodidus, Torah, prayer, and crying out to Hashem — as the true Tzaddikim have taught us.

Speech carries immensely powerful force to transform a person from bad to good, for the essential victory in life's war is achieved through speech — it is Israel's primary weapon. As our Sages taught: "Our strength is only in the mouth." And this is the essential weapon of Moshiach, which is embodied by all the true Tzaddikim in whom all of Israel are included and contained. For all the weaponry of Moshiach is solely through prayer — which operates through speech — as is written in Torah 2 of Likutay Moharan and in many other places. Through this is accomplished the essential subjugation of the ayin hara, from which comes forgetfulness. For the nullification of forgetfulness and the attainment of genuine zikharon [remembrance] come through speech — "remember by mouth" — as our Sages taught. Just as one sees with one's own eyes that by reviewing one's learning many times with full speech, one always remembers it — so too with regard to the essential remembrance described above, of the World to Come, against which the ayin hara contends, seeking to erase it from the heart: the remedy is to review this remembrance through verbal speech. One should accustom oneself each day to speak aloud, with full voice, about the matter of this zikharon — to speak to one's own heart and remind oneself in full speech: "What will become of me in the World to Come? What is my ultimate end? Did I come here to set myself up permanently in this world, G-d forbid? This world passes and races by and vanishes. I came here only to prepare myself for the World to Come." And for this purpose one must study mussar books that are founded upon the words of our Sages in the Gemara and Midrashim and upon the teachings of true Tzaddikim, for all genuine mussar books speak of the purpose of the World to Come. Likewise one must practice hisbodidus each day, speaking aloud about the purpose of the World to Come, as stated. For speech has great power to remind the person, as above. And this is the meaning of: "Whenever I speak of him, I remember him more and more" [Yirmeyahu 31:19].
